newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish T-bill trade booms on money mkt dealer plan.
newsitem.headline: Polish T-bill trade booms on money mkt dealer plan.

text.p: Trade on Poland's secondary T-bill market has nearly doubled in recent months as banks jockey for position to become eligible for operations with the central bank next year, analysts said on Monday.
In October alone turnover on the secondary T-bill market rose by 51.6 percent to 47.26 billion zlotys, while secondary turnover in NBP-bills rose by 60.7 percent to 7.36 billion.

"Banks are putting much effort to get the money market dealer status, which contributed to the significant increase of liquidity," said Jacek Osinski, deputy head of the monetary policy department at the National Bank of Poland. @

Money market dealers, to be appointed next year, will be allowed to participate in the NBP's open market operations, in primary NBP-bill tenders. The status also raises the prestige of the bank for clients.
Presently 29 banks have the status of so-called primary dealers on the basis of individual agreements with the NBP, but the central bank wants to cut their number to around 15 starting from January.

The NBP created the new money market dealer scheme, in which banks get points for activity on secondary markets, to boost non-inflationary financing of the budget deficit by the domestic non-financial sector.
The average daily portfolios of T-bills in the domestic non-banking sector rose to 8.37 billion last month from 6.37 billion zlotys in July -- when the scheme started.
At the start of the central bank's scheme in July, turnover on the secondary T-bill market was 26.19 billion and only 512 million zlotys on the NBP-bill market.
Dealers said the race for the money market dealer status may lead to a sustained high growth of secondary market trade, especially on the T-bill market.
The NBP will pick the top 15 banks to be money market dealers in 1997 in December.
